sqlparse-begin-end-semicolon.difficulty_notes: Statement splitter is a token-level state machine; must ignore ';' inside BEGIN...END while keeping 'BEGIN;' (transaction) splitting, which existing tests check.

sqlparse-tzcast-whitespace.prompt:
sqlparse.format() with reindent=True drops a space when a function argument contains AT TIME ZONE: sqlparse.format("SELECT f(HOUR from bar AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') from foo", reindent=True) returns "SELECT f(HOUR
         frombar AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')
from foo" (note 'frombar'), which is no longer valid SQL. Expected: "SELECT f(HOUR
         from bar AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')
from foo". Please fix this without changing any other behavior.
sqlparse-tzcast-whitespace.difficulty_notes: Symptom is in reindent output but the cause is an over-eager AT TIME ZONE grouping rule in engine/grouping.py that swallows the preceding whitespace; requires tracing format->grouping.

sqlparse-strip-comments-hints.prompt: sqlparse.format(sql, strip_comments=True) also removes optimizer hints, which changes what the query does. 'select --+full(u)' becomes 'select', 'SELECT /*+cluster(T)*/* FROM T_EEE T where A >:1' becomes 'SELECT  * FROM T_EEE T where A >:1', and 'insert /*+ DIRECT */ into sch.table_name as select * from foo' becomes 'insert   into sch.table_name as select * from foo'. Hints (--+, #+ and /*+ ... */) should be left exactly as written while ordinary comments are still stripped, e.g. 'select --+full(u)\n--comment simple' should become 'select --+full(u)\n'. Please fix this without changing any other behavior.
sqlparse-strip-comments-hints.difficulty_notes: Lexer already tags hints with distinct subtypes; fix needs to skip hint tokens (incl. grouped Comment nodes) in the strip filter without an infinite loop over the same index.

sqlparse-between-leading-dot-float.prompt: sqlparse mis-parses BETWEEN when the bounds are floats written without a leading zero. sqlparse.parse('a BETWEEN .03 AND .06')[0] comes out with BETWEEN and AND as Name tokens, grouped into identifiers 'a BETWEEN' and '.03 AND', instead of keywords; with '0.03' and '0.06' it parses correctly. Expected: BETWEEN and AND are keyword tokens and '.03' and '.06' are standalone Float tokens (same for lowercase 'between ... and'). Dotted names such as 'select foo.bar', 'select foo . bar' and 'select a.b.c' must still be grouped as identifiers. Please fix this without changing any other behavior.
sqlparse-between-leading-dot-float.difficulty_notes: Root cause is a lexer regex (word followed by '.') in keywords.py; must exclude a numeric literal after the dot while keeping 'schema . name' member access.

mistune-emphasis-mod3.prompt:
mistune's emphasis handling disagrees with CommonMark on some runs of asterisks. mistune.html('*a***a*') returns '

a**a*

', but the CommonMark reference implementations (commonmark.js, markdown-it) produce '

a*a

'. Likewise '*foo***bar*' gives '

foo**bar*

' instead of '

foo*bar

'. Please make mistune match CommonMark here without changing any other behavior.
mistune-emphasis-mod3.difficulty_notes: CommonMark rule-of-3 must use the original delimiter-run length, not the remaining length after partial consumption; deep in the delimiter algorithm.

mistune-table-delimiter-row.prompt:
With the table plugin enabled (mistune.create_markdown(plugins=['table'])), ordinary text that happens to contain pipes is turned into a table and a line of it disappears. Rendering 'Name | Age John | 30 Jane | 25 ' produces a table with header Name/Age and a single body row Jane/25; the 'John | 30' line is silently lost. There is no ---- delimiter row, so this isn't a table: expected output is '

Name | Age John | 30 Jane | 25

'. Please fix this without changing any other behavior; real tables must keep rendering as before.
mistune-table-delimiter-row.difficulty_notes: Header/delimiter validation in the table plugin silently accepts any cell as no-align; must reject non-dash cells but still allow empty cells used by existing tables.

mistune-list-directive-markers.difficulty_notes: Bug lives in list-item break-rule recompilation that string-replaces the first '3' in each regex, which hits a directive's '{3,}' quantifier; far from the directive code.

mistune-footnote-block-backref.prompt:
With the footnotes plugin, a footnote whose body ends with something other than a paragraph produces broken HTML. mistune.create_markdown(plugins=['footnotes'])('paragraph [^fn] [^fn]: *emph* > aaa ') renders the footnote item as '

  • emph

    aaa

    ↩

    • ' -- the closing tag is chopped. Expected: '

  • emph

    aaa

    ↩
    • '. Footnotes that end in a paragraph should render exactly as they do now. Please fix this without changing any other behavior.
mistune-footnote-block-backref.difficulty_notes:
Back-reference insertion blindly strips 4 chars assuming the item ends with '

'; needs to handle block-ending items with exact expected HTML.

boltons-indexedset-slice-after-remove.prompt: boltons.setutils.IndexedSet returns the wrong elements when sliced after an item has been removed. x = IndexedSet(range(10)); x.pop(2); list(x) is [0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9] as expected, but list(x[1:4]) gives [1, 3, 4, 5] instead of [1, 3, 4], list(x[-3:]) gives [8, 9] instead of [7, 8, 9], and list(x[2:-1]) gives [4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9] instead of [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]. Slicing a set that has had removals should give exactly the same result as slicing a freshly built IndexedSet with the same contents, for any start/stop/step. Please fix this without changing any other behavior.
boltons-indexedset-slice-after-remove.difficulty_notes: Requires understanding IndexedSet's dead-slot bookkeeping: slice bounds are translated into item_list space but islice consumes the live stream; must preserve odd negative-step semantics.

boltons-omd-copy.prompt: copy.copy() and copy.deepcopy() of a boltons OrderedMultiDict lose values. With o = OMD([('a', 1), ('a', 2), ('b', 3)]), copy.deepcopy(o).getlist('a') returns [2] instead of [1, 2], copy.copy(o).getlist('a') also returns [2], and the copies compare unequal to o. Pickling round-trips correctly. Both copies should keep every value, and a deepcopy must not share mutable values with the original. Please fix this without changing any other behavior.
boltons-omd-copy.difficulty_notes: dict subclass reduce protocol: inherited __reduce_ex__ replays dictitems via __setitem__ after __setstate__, collapsing multi-values; needs knowledge of copy/pickle internals.
